countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

universities.name: CHRIST (Deemed to be University)
universities.summary: CHRIST (Deemed to be University) is a private deemed-to-be university administered by the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate, with its central campus on Hosur Road, Bengaluru. Founded as Christ College in 1969 and declared a deemed university in 2008, it teaches about 40,000 students across humanities, sciences, commerce, management, engineering, architecture, education and law on four Bengaluru campuses plus Delhi NCR and Pune Lavasa.
universities.campusLifestyle: Teaching runs across four Bengaluru campuses - Central (Hosur Road), Kengeri, Bannerghatta Road and Yeshwanthpur - plus Delhi NCR and Pune Lavasa. CHRIST reports about 40,000 students from around 60 countries. The engineering school sits on the 78.5-acre Kengeri campus on Mysore Road, about 25 km from the Central campus. Central has a main auditorium of about 2,000 seats. Admitted students open a South Indian Bank account at the campus branch and use a smart ID card for fees and campus access.
universities.cityProfile: Bengaluru is the capital of Karnataka, on the Deccan Plateau in southern India. CHRIST's own Bangalore guide describes it as a centre of public-sector aerospace, telecommunications and defence industry and of India's software-services sector. The Central Campus is on Hosur Road near Dairy Circle in the south-east of the city. The Kengeri campus is on Mysore Road on the south-western edge, about 25 km from Central, so engineering students live and study at a distance from the main campus. The Bannerghatta Road and Yeshwanthpur campuses are also within the city. Bengaluru is served by Kempegowda International Airport, where CHRIST states it arranges pickup for new international students. The Office of International Affairs estimates living costs at up to USD 3,000-4,000 a year depending on accommodation.
universities.practicalExposure: CHRIST's engineering programmes run from the School of Engineering and Technology at the Kengeri campus, where seven B.Tech programmes - Information Technology, Mechanical, Civil, Computer Science and Engineering, Electronics and Communication, Automobile, and Electrical and Electronics - are on the National Board of Accreditation Tier I register to 30 June 2027. The B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering department lists industry partnerships with Cisco, Samsung, AWS, C-DAC, Tech Mahindra, Red Hat and Oracle for labs, workshops and research, allows paid internships from the second year and includes a semester-long internship in the final year. Kengeri also offers an Indo-German first-year B.Tech credit transfer with THWS, Germany. In business, the MBA runs dual-degree tracks with THWS (Germany), Western Michigan University and Virginia Commonwealth University (USA), and the Central Campus runs an MSc Data Analytics and AI dual degree with Steinbeis University, Germany. CHRIST hosts short-term US students through the University Study Abroad Consortium.
universities.hostelOverview: Residence halls are limited and are not guaranteed. The Office of International Affairs quotes hostel rooms at USD 600-1,000 a year depending on room type, and estimates total living costs at up to USD 3,000-4,000 a year depending on accommodation and personal spending. Hostel admission is for one year only; readmission depends on academic performance, discipline and participation. There is no mess in the residence halls. The international office helps students find rooms near campus when hostel places run out.
universities.dietarySupport: CHRIST's residence halls have no mess, so meals come from the campus cafeteria and eateries or from outside the campus. CHRIST does not publish a meal-plan price. Students living off campus cook or eat locally; the living-cost estimate of up to USD 3,000-4,000 a year from the Office of International Affairs includes food.
universities.safetyOverview: CHRIST states that its Bengaluru campuses follow the UGC guidelines on student safety and Karnataka's Public Safety (Measures) Enforcement Act, 2017, with CCTV across the campus and a security control room (080 4012 9485). Security staff are trained in first aid and fire safety. Each campus has an anti-ragging committee and squad under the UGC anti-ragging regulations.
universities.studentSupport: The Office of International Affairs (Audi Block, Central Campus; isc.admission@christuniversity.in) handles international admissions. CHRIST states it arranges airport pickup and on-campus accommodation for new arrivals, helps with FRRO registration and runs an orientation. Students must register with the FRRO within 14 working days and bring comprehensive medical insurance from home. Kengeri has its own international affairs contact.

faq.question: Is CHRIST (Deemed to be University) public or private?
faq.answer: It is a private deemed-to-be university administered by the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate (CMI). It began as Christ College in 1969, was declared a deemed university under Section 3 of the UGC Act in July 2008, and it appears on the UGC's consolidated list of deemed universities. As a deemed university it awards its own degrees rather than those of an affiliating state university.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: CHRIST states that all its courses are taught in English, with no switch to Kannada or another language later in the programme. Because of this, international applicants from non-English-speaking backgrounds must prove English ability before admission or complete CHRIST's English course first.

faq.question: What English test scores does CHRIST accept?
faq.answer: Applicants from non-English-speaking countries need either proof that the qualifying examination was taken in English, or IELTS 6.0 with no sub-score below 5.5, or TOEFL 550 (paper), 213 (computer) or 79 (iBT). Otherwise CHRIST requires its full-time Intensive English Language Course (March to May, over 320 hours, USD 400) or a part-time one-semester certificate course (June to December).

faq.question: Is my school-leaving qualification accepted for a bachelor's programme?
faq.answer: CHRIST assesses international curricula under Association of Indian Universities (AIU) stipulations. For B.Tech it states that IB applicants need 3 Higher Level and 3 Standard Level subjects with 24 credits, and GCE/Edexcel applicants need at least 3 A levels at grade C or above, alongside the programme's subject rules such as Physics and Mathematics with 50 per cent in Mathematics.

faq.question: Is there an entrance test and interview?
faq.answer: Yes for most programmes. B.Tech, MSc Clinical Psychology and MA Media and Communication Studies use a 90-minute online entrance test followed by an in-person skill assessment, 90-second micro presentation and 10-minute interview. MSc Data Science skips the test but keeps the in-person stages. The MBA uses a management test score for eligibility, then group discussion, written assessment and interview.

faq.question: Can I attend the selection process outside India?
faq.answer: For the 2026 NRI and international rounds CHRIST held the skill assessment, micro presentation and interview in Bahrain, Dubai, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Saudi Arabia as well as on its Indian campuses, with the entrance test online. The MBA 2027 cycle lists only Indian venues: Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Pune and, for Session I, Kolkata.

faq.question: How much does a programme cost for an international student?
faq.answer: Fees are published in US dollars by programme and year, in two tiers. For B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering, other foreign nationals pay USD 5,700 in years 1-2 and USD 6,200 in years 3-4 (USD 23,800 in total), while SAARC, African and ASEAN nationals and PIO/OCI holders pay USD 5,100 and USD 5,600. The MBA is USD 8,000 a year. A USD 100 registration fee is non-refundable. Hostel rooms cost USD 600-1,000 a year, and CHRIST estimates living costs at up to USD 3,000-4,000 a year.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Foreign citizens and PIO and OCI card holders apply in the International Student category through CHRIST's online admissions portal (espro.christuniversity.in/Application). Register once, choose the programme and campus, upload marks statements and pay the application fee online. Then book the entrance-test date and selection venue. International admission queries go to isc.admission@christuniversity.in.

faq.question: When do programmes start and when are applications open?
faq.answer: The academic year starts in late May or June. For 2026 the MBA and MSc Data Science were inaugurated on 25 May, the Kengeri B.Tech on 8 June and most other postgraduate programmes on 11 June. CHRIST lists the next application cycle for most programmes as opening on 8 December 2026. MBA 2027 applications are open from 5 September 2026 to 24 January 2027.

faq.question: Can I work part-time in India while studying?
faq.answer: No. The Bureau of Immigration states that foreigners on a student visa must not take up any employment or business activity in India. Budget for tuition, hostel and living costs from funds brought from home or from scholarships.

faq.question: What happens after arrival in Bengaluru?
faq.answer: CHRIST requires international students to register with the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer within 14 working days of admission or arrival. At admission it checks the passport and visa, a Medical Fitness Certificate and any Resident Permit already held. It also asks students to arrive at least seven days before classes, bring comprehensive medical insurance from home and open an account at the South Indian Bank campus branch.

faq.question: What do CHRIST's accreditations cover?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited the university A+ with CGPA 3.42 in Cycle 2, declared in October 2022. NBA's Tier I (Washington Accord) register lists seven B.Tech programmes at the Kengeri campus up to 30 June 2027. The MBA's NBA period ended on 30 June 2026 and did not appear as renewed in September 2026. NIRF 2025 ranks CHRIST 63rd among universities.

faq.question: Is on-campus accommodation guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. CHRIST states that hostel seats are limited, admission to a residence hall is for one year only, and readmission depends on performance and conduct. Rooms cost USD 600-1,000 a year depending on type, and the residence halls have no mess. The Office of International Affairs helps students find accommodation near campus.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions.
